points.point: The AI data center technology change documented in the Vault is the move from the 48 V ecosystem to 800 V / ±400 Vdc HVDC as rack power reaches MW class
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions HVDC/power density but not 48 V to 800 V / ±400 Vdc or MW-class rack shift

points.point: The Vault's AI server ecosystem → R&S solution mapping assigns VNA, oscilloscope and phase-noise instruments (ZNL/MXO/FSWP/ZNA/ZNB) to these needs, not signaling or non-signaling radio communication testers
points.label: covered
points.why: says AI server mapping uses VNA/oscilloscope/phase-noise tools, not signaling testers

points.point: Even data center power-electronics topics (800V HVDC) are mapped in the Vault to MXO / FSWP / ZISO / BMS test, with no signaling tester involvement
points.label: covered
points.why: maps HVDC/power topics to MXO/FSWP/ZISO/BMS-type tools, not signaling testers

points.point: That mapping page is only a sales/test clue from an Excel conversion and is not a formal configuration or validated requirement
points.label: missing
points.why: does not state the AI server mapping is only an Excel sales clue, not a formal validated configuration

points.point: In the Vault, signaling vs non-signaling tester roles are defined for wireless device testing: CMX500 for R&D signaling, CMP180 for production non-signaling RF
points.label: partial
points.why: covers CMX500 signaling use but omits CMP180 as production non-signaling RF role

points.point: Non-signaling mode is tied to WLAN/cellular device production RF measurement speed, i.e. a device-test driver rather than a data center driver
points.label: contradicted
points.why: claims AI data center shifts drive non-signaling waveform/TX validation instead of tying non-signaling to device production RF speed

points.point: The documented driver of new signaling-tester measurement capability is new wireless standards such as Wi-Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn
points.label: covered
points.why: identifies Wi-Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn as a driver for new signaling capability

points.point: Signaling test content in the Vault is scoped to LTE / 5G / Wi-Fi UE RF, application-layer and protocol measurements within 400 MHz–8 GHz, with no data center scope
points.label: contradicted
points.why: lists LTE/5G/Wi-Fi signaling content but presents it as affected by AI data center technology, contrary to no data-center scope

invented: AI data center technology shifts the tester requirement toward broader connectivity validation
network emulation, RF/WLAN signaling, throughput/PER/BLER, IP/application analysis, latency/jitter impairment control
generative-AI user-experience KPIs, multi-radio desense, and non-signaling waveform/TX validation
The signaling tester portion is most relevant where “connectivity” becomes wireless/network/application validation
A signaling tester used for AI application scenarios needs controlled network-condition emulation plus application-layer KPI measurement
The tester needs multi-technology, multi-channel signaling and desense capability
